defs.def: to take and use sth that belongs to sb else, and return it to them at a later time 借；借用

ex.s: “We’re not just ‘borrowing’ from different disciplines — we’re really putting them on equal footing in order to create something greater than the sum of its parts.”
ex.t: "我们不仅仅是在不同学科间'借用'——我们真正地将它们放在平等的位置上，以创造出比各部分总和更伟大的东西。"
然而，我不能让自己真正动手去做。

ex.s: Borrowed items are subject to recall by the lending library.
ex.t: 成为一名成功的画家需要果断。

ex.s: What is a rule for borrowing a print book through ILL?

The last one standing has just been turned into a “mini community library”: any passer-by can “borrow” a book from its shelves, and return it later, or replace it with another title from their own collection.
ex.t: 最后一个幸存的电话亭刚刚被改造成了一个"迷你社区图书馆"：任何路人都可以从架子上"借"一本书，之后归还，或者用自己的藏书替换。

ex.s: He wanted to borrow some love stories.
ex.t: 每周见老师D. 练习语言技能

ex.s: My love of the written word began early as my mother read to me every evening. ___32___ I started reading books on my own before age 5 and my mother took me to the public library once a week to borrow several books.
ex.t: 我对文字的热爱开始得很早，母亲每晚给我读书。___32___我不到5岁就开始自己看书，母亲每周带我一次去公共图书馆借阅几本书。

ex.s: You can borrow movies on DVDs, music on CDs, and popular magazines.
The English came across this word in India and borrowed it as touffon.
ex.t: 后来，当英国船只在中国海遇到猛烈风暴时，英国人学到了粤语词"tai fung"，意思是"大风"。这个单词与touffon的______联系纯属巧合。

defs.def: to take money from a person or bank and agree to pay it back to them at a later time 借入（款项）；（向 … ）借贷

ex.s: Another borrowed word that came about through ___35___ between two nations is gung-ho.
ex.t: 这些组织是20世纪30年代西方人在中国建立的，旨在促进工业和经济发展。

defs.def: to take words, ideas, etc. from another language, person, etc. and use them, as your own 引用，借用（思想、言语等）

ex.s: “There was once a town in the heart of America, ___44___ all life seemed to enjoy peaceful existence with is surroundings,” her fable begins, ___45___ (borrow) some familiar words from many age-old fables.
ex.t: “从前，在美国的心脏地带有一座小镇，___44___那里所有的生命似乎都与其周围环境和平安宁地共存，”她的寓言这样开头，___45___（borrow）借用了许多古老寓言中一些熟悉的字句。

ex.s: On a recent program, we told you the stories of English words borrowed from other languages.
ex.t: 它们最常来自粤语或其他汉语方言而不是普通话。

ex.s: Many of the Chinese words that are now part of English were borrowed long ago.
ex.t: 英语单词kowtow是一个动词，意思是过于轻易地同意做别人要你做的事，或者以一种显得______的方式服从有权势的人。

defs.def: to still be alive after the time when you were expected to die 活过寿限；大限已近

ex.s: English has borrowed many words from other languages.
ex.t: 英语从其他语言中借用了许多词。

ex.s: The performance borrowed a lot from Chinese dance and music, so the Eastern influence on the ballet was clear.
ex.t: 这部作品大量借鉴了中国舞蹈和音乐，因此东方对该芭蕾舞的影响显而易见。

ex.s: In 1924, he creatively borrowed “youmo” from Ancient Chinese as the translation for the English word “humour”.
ex.t: 1924年，他创造性地借用古汉语中的“幽默”作为英语单词“humour”的译文。

ex.s: And even if we could remember a number and needed to call it urgently, it would still be more convenient to borrow a mobile phone from someone else than walk around looking for a phone box.
ex.t: 而且即使我们能记住号码且急需拨打，向别人借一部手机也比到处找电话亭更方便。

ex.s: For most of this history, lenders relied mainly on their subjective judgement when deciding whether or not a borrower was creditworthy.
ex.t: 在这段历史的大部分时间里，放贷人主要依赖主观判断来决定借款人是否值得授信。

defs.def: to be doing sth that other people are likely to soon stop you from doing 做很快就会遭到制止的事；好景不长
